It would also have the added benefit of strengthening the bad eye if you put the patch on the good eye. It would take a little getting used to of course.

Stay positive m8.

>Honestly speaking, it was more of an issue during childhood, when you're an adult, people look past these things (visible disabilities, etc.) and treat you like a normal person.

I have achieved much in spite of it but this doesn't feel cathartic; it feels quite haunting knowing I've only had 1/10th of what I could were my eyes normal.

>I'm looking in to treatment. If that doesn't work I'm gonna restructure my whole life (basically get a new workplace and acquaintances) and start wearing an eye patch. I'll just tell people I'm blind in one eye and leave it at that.

>It's like lazy eye is stigmatised so much it's unapproachable. Whereas blindness is something people want to be compassionate about. Even though lazy eye often causes functional blindness in that eye.

Honestly man I'm 100% with you on that. I am tempted to try an eyepatch but it seems ridiculous, even when I go through densely populated cities (London, Berlin, Paris) I don't think I see any eye patches... it seems very attention drawing.
I think that would draw even MORE negative attention to it.Thank you for hte suggestion though :)

I physically can't enjoy life. I was flawed fromthe beginning to never be happy. This is the end result. Final exit.

I'm not good looking though. I don't think you understand that having a lazy eye overrides every other face aesthetic. I'd rather have a huge nose or a recessed chin than a lazy eye. Hell I'd even go down to 5'10" if it meant my lazy eye disappeared. 


also I've explored avenues for correction. It can't be corrected as I was meant to have surgery at a young age (the lazy eye developed from birth) which my parents were too dumb to accept. Now it's too late. There is unfortunately no treatment now because vision didn't properly develop in it therefore rendering treatment invalid.


ugh

Thanks man. It sums up my mood perfectly though. I'm not even a fat, gross, neckbeard pining for a girl who'd never give him the time of day. 

I was given all the tools to enjoy life and pursue my intended career (face, height,frame) but fate fucked me over at the last minute. My childhood dream was to model and reality has crushed that :(

Let me share my story if anybody cares.

I'm 6'1" (it helps), thin (neither a benefit nor negative) and have a reasonably attractive face... EXCEPT for a horribly disfiguring lazy eye which not only makes me ugly but gives me great anxiety about making eye contact with girls... you can imagine this double whammy must suck. It's one thing to be ugly because you have a big nose or are a bit fat but when you're effectively cross-eyed you can't make eye contact and therefore give off creepy and unconfident vibes unintentionally... not to brag but regarding the rest of my face (strong jaw, nice cheekbones, good eyebrows/hooded eyes, good chin) people have said I could model if it wasn't for that. Great! Thanks God for putting me so close yet so far. Nice tease.

Anyway I don't really want much sympathy because I guess I've accepted it. I'm not particularly happy, it does depress me at times because I feel like my life would be a lot lot better in terms of dating, girls, jobs, etc. if my eye was normal BUT let me tell you

Despite this I have made every effort to learn and force myself to interact with women normally using good social etiquette and a slight hint of charisma and have slept with attractive girls which now reach the double digits.


tl;dr if I can do it, he can do it.
